headline: Back-to-back long runs across 48 hours cap a +16% volume block, while aerobic efficiency at easy effort continues to improve meaningfully.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The two-day sequence finishing today — a moderate aerobic run followed by an 18 km effort the next morning — is the most relevant data point right now. Back-to-back durability is a core ultra competency, and completing that kind of stacked load on the tail end of a volume block that's already up significantly on the prior four weeks signals genuine readiness, not just accumulated mileage. The fact that easy-run HR has dropped noticeably across comparable efforts over the same period reinforces that this volume increase is being absorbed, not just survived.

The June 27th threshold effort sits clearly apart from everything else in recent weeks — a hard, fast session that demonstrated the speed end of your capacity is still sharp. That session combined with the current aerobic efficiency trend suggests both ends of your range are in good shape simultaneously, which is the defining characteristic of functional hybrid fitness.

Strength frequency has dipped slightly relative to the prior block, which is worth noting but not alarming given the running load increase. The two qualities are genuinely competing for recovery resource right now, and the running side has clearly been prioritised. The 20-week running streak — now matching your all-time best — is a marker of consistency worth recognising without over-indexing on it.
watch_items: Monitor whether easy-run HR continues its downward trend or plateaus — a plateau here after this volume block would be normal and expected
Watch how strength sessions feel over the next 1–2 weeks given the accumulated running load; quality of movement is a more useful signal than session count
Pay attention to how quickly you recover from the back-to-back — the recovery arc after stacked efforts is informative data for future ultra pacing strategy
If volume consolidates slightly this week, treat it as part of the block structure rather than a break in momentum

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 145 km vs 125 km prior block (+16%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
